what.heading: What is a string?
paragraphs: A string is text inside quotes. Text from a PDF often arrives messy, with extra spaces or odd capitals, and you'll clean it before you use it. You'll also build AI prompts by placing text inside a longer string.

points.title: Slicing
points.text: `text[0:4]` takes the characters at positions 0 to 3.

example.heading: What slicing looks like
example.caption: `date_text[0:4]` takes positions 0, 1, 2 and 3, so `year` is "2025". The end number, 4, is left out.

demos.label: Clean messy text
demos.code:
raw = "  Effective Date: 2025-03-21  "
clean = raw.strip()
print(clean)
print(clean.replace("Effective Date: ", ""))
demos.note: .strip() removes spaces at both ends. .replace(old, new) swaps one piece of text for another; an empty "" removes it.

demos.label: Change capitals
demos.code:
doc_type = "Certificate of Quality"
print(doc_type.upper())
print(doc_type.lower())
found = "COVER LETTER"
print(found.lower() == "Cover Letter".lower())
demos.note: Lowering both sides before you compare them means capital letters no longer matter.

demos.label: Slice and split
demos.code:
date_text = "2025-03-21"
print(date_text[0:4])
print(date_text[5:7])
print(date_text.split("-"))
print("Lot AB-4417  Exp 2027".split())
demos.note: .split("-") cuts at each dash. With nothing inside the brackets, .split() cuts at spaces.

demos.label: A multi-line prompt
demos.code:
page_text = "Certificate of Quality. Lot AB-4417."
prompt = f"""Classify this page.
Return JSON like this:
{{"doc_type": "<type>"}}

Page text:
{page_text}"""
print(prompt)
demos.note: Three quotes let a string run over several lines. {page_text} gets filled in. {{ and }} print as one real { and }.

try.prompt: Clean `raw_lot` into `lot` (no spaces, capital letters: "AB-4417"). Then turn the prompt into an f-string: add `f` before the three quotes, put `{lot}` where it says LOT, and double the JSON braces to `{{` and `}}` so they stay as real braces. (Single braces there stop the code with a ValueError.)
try.starter:
raw_lot = "  ab-4417  "
lot = raw_lot

prompt = """Find the expiry date for lot LOT.
Return JSON: {"expiry": "YYYY-MM-DD"}"""
print(prompt)
try.solution:
raw_lot = "  ab-4417  "
lot = raw_lot.strip().upper()

prompt = f"""Find the expiry date for lot {lot}.
Return JSON: {{"expiry": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}"""
print(prompt)

checks.hint: lot should be "AB-4417". Use .strip() to remove the spaces and .upper() for capital letters. String methods give back a new string, so store the result: lot = raw_lot.strip().upper().
Your prompt still says LOT. Replace that word with {lot} inside the string.
Your prompt shows {lot} as plain text. Put the letter f right before the three opening quotes (f"""...), and keep single braces around {lot}.
The first line of the prompt should end with "lot AB-4417.". Check that {lot} sits right after the word lot and before the full stop.
The printed prompt should show one { and one } around the JSON. In an f-string, write {{ to get { and }} to get }.

try.expect_stdout:
Find the expiry date for lot AB-4417.
Return JSON: {"expiry": "YYYY-MM-DD"}
try.stdout_hint: Your prompt is right, but it isn't printed. Keep print(prompt) at the end.
